newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to overhaul statistics system for EU.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to overhaul statistics system for EU.

text.p: Hungary plans to upgrade its statistical system for enterprises and agriculture in preparation for European Union (EU) membership, the Central Statistical Office (KSH) said on Tuesday.
Hungary is one of the central eastern European countries, which hope to become EU members in the years following 2000.
The KSH plans to set up a detailed database about Hungary's 1.1 million enterprises by September 30, KSH vice-president Miklos Balogh told a news conference.

"(With the registration) our system will be comparable with those of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) and the EU," the KSH said in a statement. "This is the statistical condition of joining (the EU)."

Currently four government agencies collect data about enterprises and the number of those which are likely to have ceased their operations is estimated at 300,000, but the government does not have precise figures, Balogh said.
Hungary also plans to upgrade its agricultural registration system by early 1999, KSH vice-president Peter Pukli said.
EU statistics and agricultural subsidies are based on calculations of value added to products, while the Hungarian statistical system does not yet have this category, he said.

Agricultural subsidies are believed to become one of the most controversial issues during EU membership talks for Hungary, which has substantial agricultural exports and trade surpluses in this sector.

Pukli said the planned change would improve the position of Hungarian producers, who often complain that under the current statistical system only part of the agricultural subsidies approved by parliament are distributed to them.
